# Starboard Protocol

> Starboard is an open, deterministic "rules of the road" for satellites: a
> collision-avoidance and give-way protocol in which two spacecraft from rival
> operators, with no radio contact, independently compute the identical
> verdict (bit for bit) about which one maneuvers. Like the maritime COLREGS
> starboard rule, but for orbit. Open specification (CC BY 4.0), reference
> code (AGPL-3.0, commercial license available).

Key facts:

- Input: standard CCSDS 508.0-B-1 Conjunction Data Messages (CDMs), parsed
  with an exact, libc-independent decimal ingest so every implementation
  gets identical bits.
- Decision: covariance-aware probability of collision (Patera contour
  integral), then five rules in order: capability, tier, overtaking,
  starboard, fair coin. The rules are evaluated on a canonical pair ordering,
  which makes agreement true by construction (Theorem 1, machine-checked with
  CBMC).
- Action: a minimum-delta-v Clohessy-Wiltshire burn, exactly reversible back
  to the slot. If both craft wrongly maneuver, their burns add separation
  (Theorem 2).
- Flock (Layer 4): maneuver notices spread hop by hop over inter-satellite
  links; every craft keeps the same ledger of who is moving and checks movers'
  paths against its own. It warns; it never decides.
- Flight software: C99 library, 43 KB code, no heap, no recursion,
  built-in self-test, SEU-tolerant redundant evaluation, CCSDS telemetry.
- Evidence: bit-identical transcripts across gcc/clang, C++/C, 11 CPU
  architectures (x86, ARM, RAD750-class PowerPC, RISC-V, SPARC, MIPS, s390x)
  and bare-metal Cortex-M3/M4F/M7; fuzzing (~129M executions); found a
  misrounding in ARM soft-float double addition (libgcc __aeabi_dadd) and
  ships a verified replacement.
- Status: verified in software and emulation; not yet flown or tested on
  flight hardware.
